not a big complainer. Over the years I've had excellent care at Field head, especially when the great Dr Faulkner looked after me. The desk staff have been fine for me - often helpful & constructive.
But latterly there are two areas that have made life more difficult:
1. Patchs . I accept it works for some but one size doesn't fit all and as for the claim (from.its website) " I want to see a GP
Get care in minutes" it made me laugh. Patchs is a private limited company, no doubt with a lucrative NHS contract, that puts up another barrier between the patient and the GP. For me it invariably adds days and even weeks to the appointment time. Its bureaucracy makes me reluctant to contact the surgery and this can't be a good thing - delay usually means a worse outcome.
2. Prescriptions. 48 hours possible delay? How about 4/5 DAYS delay? I have become used to my Friday request for repeat meds not being dealt with until the following Friday (  I usually ring the pharmacy on Friday morning to check as a further weekend delay is unsafe) but this week I had clear evidence of delay from the surgery, not from the pharmacy. GP phoned me last Monday: blood test shows significant anaemia so iron pills prescribed there and then. Today (Thursday) pharmacist has just received the prescription & will.fulfill.the.request.on Friday as they need to order the pills. Why was the order not sent on Monday? It must be a routine press of a button. In my case the delay isn't life or death (but it will be 4 days of avoidable chronic fatigue) and for others such a delay could be painful/ damaging/ anxiety-inducing - all avoidable.
Is it too much to ask the surgery to get the meds out to patients in a timely fashion?
